title: GSIM: Accelerating RTL Simulation for Large-Scale Designs
problem: Software RTL simulation is a major bottleneck in hardware design; simulation of complex processors and systems exhibits high computational overhead in multiple layers (supernode, node, and bit levels).
motivation: RTL simulation is essential for design exploration, verification, and preliminary performance evaluation, but slow simulation blocks rapid iteration on large designs like modern processors.
method: GSIM identifies and optimizes computational overhead across three levels: supernode-level optimizations for high-level logic, node-level techniques for gate-level operations, and bit-level optimizations for bitwise computation. Combines these with efficient data structures and scheduling to accelerate simulation of complex processors.
key_novelty: First RTL simulator optimizing across multiple abstraction levels (supernode/node/bit) simultaneously, demonstrating 19.94× speedup on realistic processor workloads.
contributions: Multi-level optimization framework for RTL simulation (supernode, node, bit)
Efficient data structures and scheduling for large-scale designs
Successful simulation of XiangShan RISC-V processor
7.34× speedup for Linux boot on XiangShan vs. Verilator
primary_theme: Multi-level RTL simulation acceleration for large-scale processor design
